text: Grandfather Ghondor, or simply named Ghondor (Japanese: , Gondō), is a character in .
Grand Marshal (Japanese: , Gurandosorujā, Grand Soldier) is a Kevesi Defender class in and . __TOC__
Graffiti Hint A is a Key Item in . It is obtained upon starting If Walls Could Speak. It is written in Old Alrestian.
Graffiti Hint B is a Key Item in . It is obtained from the graffiti on the wall at the Echoes of Gran Dell Citadel during If Walls Could Speak. It is written in Old Alrestian.
Graffiti Hint C is a Key Item in . It is obtained from the graffiti on the wall at the Argan Cathedral Ruins during If Walls Could Speak. It is written in Old Alrestian.
Graffiti Hint D is a Key Item in . It is obtained from the graffiti on a wall in Vermilion Woods during If Walls Could Speak. It is written in Old Alrestian.
The Growth Reset Kit is a Key Item in . It allows the Affinity Growth of a character to be reset, refunding any Affinity Points spent. It can be found by Declessa Altar on the Aurora Shelf.
Guguru is a Nopon NPC in . Guguru's Community is gained when talking to him after completing The Very Lost Nopon, talking with him twice, and changing Babalulu's Community status.

Gramps is a Field Track from , composed by ACE. It is track eighteen of disc three from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track eighteen of disc eight from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. The song plays during the day in Fonsett Village. This track also plays during the day On Gramps's Back, but can only be heard there if the player uses a secret instant-death code after the battle against the King Crustip in order to warp Rex back to the area.

Grand Theater of Life is a track from , composed by Manami Kiyota and Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track five of disc eight from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track five of disc nineteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the cutscene where the party confronts Z in the Amphitheater before the start of the final battle.

The Grav Eagle Seidr (Japanese: グラビイーグル・バスギア, Gurabiīguru basugia) is Story Exclusive Enemy in . It is a Seidr Ganglion machine. It can be found at level 48 around the Lifehold Core in the Cauldros Waters during Chapter 12. It is always flanked by two Galdr variants.

Grenada Pilot (Male) is a Holofigure in . It depicts a male mannequin wearing the complete Liesel's Bodywear series. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Affinity Mission New Skell on the Block.
Grenada Maintenance (M) is a Holofigure in . It depicts a male mannequin wearing the complete Maintenance Wear I series. It is obtained as a reward for completing The Skell License.

Gu Galda (Japanese: , Gu Garuda) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a level 39 Wrothian and is fought alongside Gi Bordo, Da Dorde, Zo Zongra in Sylvalum during the squad mission The Wrothian Four.

Hades Beetles (Japanese: , Narakunomizusumashi) are collectables in . They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they have a black hue that is so dark that someone is being drawn into an abyss. Five are required for Secret Elixir Ingredients.

Hard Lotuses (Japanese: , Hādo Houren) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they are green and surprisingly spicy, with the burn being felt soon after eating them. Three are required for Reversed Tastes.

Happy Ducks (Japanese: , Tanoshiikamo) are collectables in . They can be found in Bionis' Interior. According to their description, it is a duck with an infectiously gleeful quack that brings delight to all.

Heart Peaches (Japanese: , Hāto Pīchi) are collectables in and . They can be found in Alcamoth and Colony 6. According to their description, they are peaches that are warm to the touch and they are often eaten before declaring someone's love. Five are required for Getting to Know Dorothy.

Ha Ha Has (Japanese: , Mofumofumofumoufu) are collectables in and . They can be found in Alcamoth. According to their description, Riki seemed to had fun when he named them and they are furry white creatures of some kind.

Happy Rabbits (Japanese: , Happī Usagi) are collectables in . They can be found in Tephra Cave. According to their description, they are rabbits with cute yellow eyes and they say touching them brings happiness. Four are required for Decoration Makeover.

Happy Carnivals (Japanese: , Yukai Kānibaru) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Satorl Marsh. According to their description, Reyn was laughing when he named them and they are a weird liquid that chimes when stirred.

Heavy Armour (Japanese: , Jūsōbi) tends towards high weight, high Physical Defence and low Ether Defence. It can only be worn by characters who have the Heavy Equipment skill, or through Skill Links at a cost of 15 (Riki and Dunban) or 30 (Reyn and Sharla) Affinity Coins. No characters have this skill unlocked initially, though it is fairly easy for Reyn to learn it. Melia's Heavy Armour Mastery skill effectively adds 30 to the Ether Defence values for all Heavy equipment. Heavy Armours have three general designs as represented by Ledios, M100, and Rex. All heavy equipment shares a general appearance with one of the three, with several colour variants of each.

The Heart of the Giants is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is one of the three treasures of the Giants, the other two being Truth of the Giants and Daring of the Giants. These three items are required to open the door at Three Sage Summit, and are required for The Giants' Treasures and The Final Giants' Ruins. The Heart of the Giants can be obtained by completing the following chain of quests which become available after completing Kind Lupa's Grampypon and Secret Elixir Ingredients: * Mystery of Makna Ruins 1 * Mystery of Makna Ruins 2 * Mystery of Makna Ruins 3 * Mystery of Makna Ruins 4

Heavy Bunniv Irons are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Iron Bunnivs and the Mining Patrichev in Tephra Cave. According to their description, they are the iron of choice for Bunnivs and they can not sleep at night without them. Two pieces of it are needed for Education-Crazy Suzanna.
Haste (Japanese: , Heisuto) is a Gem in and that increases the rate of Auto-Attacks. Haste also changes party AI behavior by decreasing the time between their use of Battle Arts. __TOC__

Hazzai Cape (Japanese: , Hazzai Misaki) is a location in . It is located in Colony 9. It is a small peninsula east of Outlook Park, south of Agora Shore, and on the other side of Anti-Air Battery 3. It can only be reached by swimming, most quickly from the bridge between the Central Plaza and the Residential District (there is a gap in the railings about half way across). In early stages of the game it can be difficult to reach, as level 70 Throne Sardi patrol the nearby waters. However on the cape itself there are only low level Krabbles (Stone and Marble) during the day, although at night the Stone Krabbles are replaced with Solid Krabbles. The Impenetrable Redrob is also here at night, si

Heavy Gear (Japanese: , Kyōkagata Gia) is heavy head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Bad Timing and from several shops. It is not dropped by any enemies. It is made by Homs with anti-Mechon enhancements.

Heavy Gauntlets are heavy arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made by Homs with anti-Mechon enhancements. They are not dropped by any enemies but can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Cook-Off Comeback? and can be bought at several shops for 14,000 G.
Heavy Leggings are heavy legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Homs leggings built with anti-Mechon enhancements.

Heavy Boots are heavy feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made for Homs and have anti-Mechon enhancements. They can be bought at Sword Valley for 21,000 G, and can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Cook-Off Final Blow?!.

Hand Bunnits (Japanese: , Hando Banitto) are enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family. They can be found in the lower part of Tephra Hill in Colony 9. Two of them must be defeated to complete Monster Quest 3 - Part 1.

Hammer Beat (Japanese: , Hanmā Bīto) is one of Reyn's physical arts in . It is a small target-area attack, meaning other targets (usually small ones) can be affected when they are within the attack radius from the target. It also generates volatile aggro equal to 25 × (Reyn's level + 14). Nene uses this art in .

Heavy Brogs (Japanese: , Hevī Guroggu) are enemies in . They are members of the Brog family, and can be found at level 38-39 on Agora Shore and in a cave near Cliff Lake in Colony 9. They can drop the Laughing Brog Bags needed for Désirée's Apology.
The Heavy Hoof is a common material item in . It can only be obtained from the Plain Armu in Colony 9.
H Speed Goggles (Japanese: , H Supīdo Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be bought at the Machina Refuge.

The Heavy Machine Depot (Japanese: , Ōgataki Hatchakujō) is a landmark in . It is located northeast of the Control Tower and west of the Port Access Pathway in Sword Valley. At this particular landmark Mumkhar - or Metal Face - is faced for the last time. During this fight he is holding a new green spear that can "decompose any life born of Bionis". After he is defeated, despite missing an arm and having been beaten, he runs at Shulk and Dunban, yelling "Just die!" Shulk then has a vision in which a spiked piece of metal falls from the fortress and impales the Faced Mechon through the chest. Shulk shouts at Mumkhar to stay back but he is ignored, and the vision comes true. The whole depot ce

The Heavenly Window (Japanese: , Jihi no Tenmado) is a Secret Area in . It is located on the third floor of Tephra Cave, reachable only after the story events at the Mechonis Core. It is reached by travelling from Vilia Lake through a now-unblocked passage to the north. The path circles around, through the Bone Corridor, to the Heavenly Window.

Happiness Fliers (Japanese: , Hapinesu Furaia) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Flier family, and can be found around level 52 - 54 near the Giant Mechon Debris on the Fallen Arm, as well as Digits 2 and 3. They only appear on sunny days. They are the only enemies that drop Flier Bloom Scales, two of which are needed for Resolution - Father.
Hazzard Driver (Japanese: , Hazādobankā) is a gunlance in , usable by Reyn. It is not effective against Mechon.
A Heavy Driver (Japanese: , Hevīgādā) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn. It is not dropped by any enemies, but can be bought or traded for.
The Half-Bloom Striker (Japanese: , Gobuzaki no Tachi) is a weapon in . It is a sword for Dunban.
Havoc Snipers (Japanese: , Katasutorosunaipu, Catastro Sniper) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are ether rifles wielded by Sharla, and can only be acquired from one shop in Colony 6.
Hero Biters (Japanese: , Yūsha no Kamukamu) are weapons in . They are biters wielded by Riki.
The Hall of Spirits (Japanese: , Eiyū-tachi no Ma) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of the High Entia Tomb.

The Hall of Trials (Japanese: , Shiren no Ma) is a location in . It is located in the High Entia Tomb. It is above the Tower of Trials, which is guarded by an Orluga Rufus on each level. It can be reached by walking east from the Hall of Spirits or the Tower of Trials - Bridge (and then walking up the levels), or west from the Ceremony Hall. A Heart-to-Heart - "Hopes and Plans" - is located here.

Healing the Healer (Japanese: , Isha no Fuyōjō) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Npa in the Underground Store of Frontier Village. If Fiora is in the active party, she will comment. Once the second objective is done, talking back to Yusa, the quest Legendary Nopon Charm will be triggered and must be first finished.
Heal Bullet (Japanese: , Hīru Baretto) is one of Sharla's Ether arts in . It recovers a portion of HP to one party member. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Healy Bullet.
Heal Blast (Japanese: , Hīru Burasuto) is one of Sharla's Ether arts in . It restores a large amount of HP to one party member. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Healy Kaboom.

Healing Gift (Japanese: , Hīrugifuto) is one of Melia's support arts in and . It sacrifices 20% of her maximum HP to heal an ally. The amount of HP restored to the ally is a percentage of Melia's max HP.

Heat Sink (Japanese: , Hīto Shinku) is a Gem in that reduces the amount by which Sharla and Kino's Talent Gauges are filled when using auto-attacks and arts. It is only effective on Sharla and Kino's ether rifles, and does not affect the duration of their Cool Off and Doze Off talent arts. In , these can be mined from the Ether Crystal deposit north of Agni's Birthplace. __TOC__

hacked location]] Hacked Locations are areas in which are either unused, or used only in cutscenes or battles, and which otherwise can only be accessed by means of hacks or cheat codes. Since all cutscenes are rendered in-engine and not pre-rendered, each cutscene makes use of an actual map in the game's files. There are a few areas that are only seen in cutscenes and cannot be reached by the player; some of them are modified versions of playable areas, and some of them may have been intended to be playable at one point during development before they were relegated to a cutscene. One area is only used as the location for one battle, and two others do not appear to be used in any cutscenes or

Head Shot (Japanese: , Heddo Sunaipu, Head Snipe) is one of Sharla's physical arts in . It guarantees a Critical Hit and has a 15% chance to cause Instant Death to a Dazed enemy. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Noggin Shot.

Heal Round (Japanese: , Hīru Raundo) is one of Sharla's Ether arts in . Sharla fires a bullet that scatters Ether, restoring a small amount of HP to the entire party. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Heal Round-a-Round.

Head Shaker (Japanese: , Heddo Sheikā) is one of Sharla's physical arts in . Sharla pistol whips an enemy, inflicting damage. If used on a Toppled enemy, it inflicts Daze. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Egg Shaker.
Helwerthia Drones are Mechonis Drones in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Heat Bullet (Japanese: , Hīto Baretto) is one of Sharla's support arts in . Sharla fires a special Ether Bullet at a party member which raises the tension of all party members within its area of effect. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Toasty-Hot Bullet.

Heat Haze (Japanese: , Kagerō) is one of Dunban's arts in . When activated, an aura activates that causes Dunban to lose all aggro, and all attacks become guaranteed to become critical hits while the Aura remains active.

Happy Happy (Japanese: , Yorokobe mo) is one of Riki's support arts in . When he activates the art, a certain percentage is added to the Party Gauge. The art can only be used when Riki's tension is high or very high.

Heal Counter (Japanese: , Hīru Kauntā) is one of Sharla's support arts in . It generates a special barrier around one party member, giving that person a Damage Heal effect. Each time that person is hit by an enemy, the field will restore 5% of their max HP. This effect lasts for a certain amount of time or a certain number of hits, whichever comes first; both the duration and the number of hits depend on the art's level. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Healy Counter.

Hanz Pods (Japanese: , Hanzu Poddo) are stationary enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Pods, and can be found at level 90 in Tephra Cave between the Heavenly Window and the Arachno Queen's Nest. They release Panasowa Arachnos. Two Hanz Pods can also be found next to Plump Sprahda, and these one release two level 95 Jadals Arachno each instead.

Hard Hoxes (Japanese: , Hādo Hoggusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Hox family, and can be found from level 13 to 16 along the Splintered Path in Colony 6 before the events at Mechonis Core, then south of Pod Depot after these events.

Hasal Apis (Japanese: , Hasaru Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Apis family, and can be found at level 30 near the Divine Sanctuary and Lakeside in Makna Forest. They can drop the Royal Apis Nectar needed for one route of Popularity Premonition.

The Health Amulet is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. Finding it is the objective of Search Quest 4 in Alcamoth. It can be found southeast of the Fountain of Hope in Alcamoth, near a small bridge. It is a Nopon charm.
Heir to the Monado (Japanese: , Monado no Kōkeisha) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Refugee Camp on the Bionis' Leg, between Reyn and Dunban at green affinity.

Harriers is a division within BLADE. Their goal is to defeat dangerous monsters. This division is known as Avalanche (Japanese: , Avaranchi) in the Japanese version. Harriers receive increased Division Points from defeating enemies, particularly Tyrants. Receiving division support from Harriers grants Melee Master, which increases damage of melee weapons.

The Headwater Cliff (Japanese: , Suigengan no Gake) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, at the southern part of Headwater Summit, on a cliff overlooking Biahno Lake and reachable from FN Site 104. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("The View From Headwater Cliff").

The Hangar (Japanese: , Hangā) is a landmark in . It is located in the Administrative District area of New Los Angeles, on the lower deck. A service elevator allows transportation between decks, while a road exit allows walking to other districts.

Hermit Tectinsulas (Japanese: , Hāmitto Tapenta) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Tectinsulas and can be found at level 12-20 at the northern end of the Sapphire Table or at Humdrum Peaks in Noctilum. They are often hidden, resembling mounds of the surrounding foliage.

Hayreddin, the Territorial (Japanese: , Nawabari Haireddin) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Simius and can be found at level 81 on East Gate Plain in Primordia. During the day, it can be found wandering near the shore, and at night it can be found sleeping atop a rock formation along with other simius. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Hayreddin, the Territorial. Its Enraged aura grants it Invincible status. Hayreddin, the Territorial will gain the buff after about ten seconds in battle.
Heavy Hitter is a Soul Voice in . It is activated when a party member lands a Critical Hit.

Hallowed Progen (Japanese: , Hōrī Ekuusu, Holy Equus) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Progen and can be found at level 21-22, level 25, or level 29-30 at Middle Hushflood, Bident Crossing, and at the upper level of Rustpool Banks in Noctilum. They can drop the Ornate Progen Horn needed for From Idea to Inventory.

Headwater Cavern (Japanese: , Suigen Dōkutsu) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave located in Primordia, northwest of Biahno Lake. Dadapon's Sunglasses and Senirapa Water can be found here during The Ties That Bind and Circle of Life respectively.

Hermit Ictuses (Japanese: , Hāmitto Manda) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Ictus family, and can be found at level 51-90 in Sylvalum, specifically at level 56 in Banshee Cave and at level 81-83 at Delusians North Summit during spore weather. Defeating four of them is required to complete the Basic Mission Ictus Infestation (Hermit).

The Headwater Summit (Japanese: , Suigengan no Sanchō) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a clifftop with a lake that feeds a river, located in Primordia, directly west and above of Biahno Lake. A landbridge connects it to Fallshorn Isle, and it must be visited during Alien Nation and The Lurker.
Hardheart Ravine BC (Japanese: , Mujō no Keikoku BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE base camp located in Sylvalum, in the Hardheart Canyon.

Haoma Scirpos (Japanese: , Haoma Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scirpo family, and can be found at level 35-40 around FN Site 406, Badr Basin, South Silent Sandsea, and Samuel Incline in Sylvalum.

Hephaestus, the Absconder (Japanese: , Chikuden no Barukan) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Duoguill family. It can be found at level 25 at East Gate Plain in Primordia during the night, northeast of Roof Rock. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Hephaestus, the Absconder. It also must be defeated for Squad Mission No.15.
Hair Trigger is a Support Art in . It grants the user Supercharge effect which makes the next Battle Art stronger.
Heradot is a Ma-non NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found above the Deck of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.

Heatproof Inox Pipes (Japanese: , Chōtainetsu Sutenresu Haikan) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Primordia, in particular around the Cliffside Beach. Three are required for the Normal Mission Better Latte Than Never.

Harnenga Cottons (Japanese: , Harunenga no Wata) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, near FN Site 204. One Harnenga Cotton is needed for the mission A Tip of the Cap.

Hemp Wallets (Japanese: , Happa no Saifu) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in the northwestern part of Primordia, in particular Stickstone Rise, Unicorn Rock, or northwestern Primordia Waters.
Hard Skins (Japanese: , Hādā Sukin) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum. Four of them are needed for Thick-Skinned.

Hello Transmitters (Japanese: , Kodoku no Moshimoshi Sōshinki) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum. Often found in Sylvalum Searoad (fast travel North Hardheart Canyon).

Hellion Blattas (Japanese: , Herion Buratta) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 43-45 in various locations in Cauldros, including at FN Sites 504 and 507.
Hazmat Hunt is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from BLADE HQ and the primary destination is Primordia.

Heidi, the Lively (Japanese: , Yakudō no Heidi) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Ovis family. It can be found at level 60 in Noctilum at Narcissus Tree, accompanied by Claire, the Sheltered and Pyotr, the Shepherd.
A Hamburger is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is needed as a bargaining tool with Aganeba during the course of The Pip-Squeak.
Hell Blattas (Japanese: , Heru Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 51-60 near FN Site 110 in Primordia.

Hell Gerrids (Japanese: , Heru Girafa) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Gerrid family, and can be found at level 58 in Quay Hollows in Sylvalum. They take a while to spawn.

The Hermit Insidias (Japanese: , Hāmitto Parako) are three Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Insidia family and are fought at level 15 on the North Coast in Oblivia during the Affinity Mission Meeting Yelv.
Hellhound is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Winged Viper at rank 10. Cross, Elma, Phog and Murderess can use this skill.
Healing Aura is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Samurai Gunner at rank 5. Cross and Gwin can use this skill.
Heatseeker is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Bastion Warrior at rank 3.
Harvey (Japanese: , Hāvi) is a Human in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a corrupt member of the Prospectors, and is fought as the boss of Special Delivery.
Hazard Shrads (Japanese: , Hazādo Zuttā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Shrad machines, and can be found at level 44-46 in Badr Stronghold in Sylvalum.
Here Come the Brides (Japanese: , Baiasu no Kekkonshiki, The Prone Wedding) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be accepted from the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship.

Heptana Logur is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Tree Clan Prone and can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles. During Here Come the Brides A route she is found at Primordia's West Gate Plain.
Healing Touch is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Enforcer at rank 9. Cross and Irina can use this skill.

Han'barac (Japanese: , Hanboiton) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is one of many Orphe born after the Normal Mission Circle of Life and he can be found south of BLADE Tower in the Administrative District. At the end of Going Viral, he will be at the north side of the Commercial District's West Melville Street. After said mission is completed, he will be located outside the Mimeosome Maintenance Center in the Administrative District.

Heinous Blattas (Japanese: , Heinesu Buratta) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 13-14 in Noctilum's Vitriol Cesspool during The Mad Monk, a location that must be defended from their attack.

Heinous Forfexes (Japanese: , Heinesu Pagurusu) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family. They can be found at level 17-19 in Noctilum's Vitriol Cesspool during The Mad Monk, a location that must be defended from their attack.
Hala Gorida (Japanese: , Heren Gorido) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.
The Hazardous Fuel Cell is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is acquired from Graham during A Dubious Operation.
The Hazardous Container is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is received from Jeffrey at the Hangar in the Administrative District during A Dubious Operation.
Hard Pom Poms are common materials in . They can be obtained from the tails of brown Ovis in Oblivia. Three are required for The Scrubdown.

Herbivores, Unite! (Japanese: , Sōgorikai, Mutual Understanding) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Naza Tenpanzi in the north end of Deliverance Park in the Residential District of New Los Angeles. The Basic Mission Tree Lovers Only can be used to locate this mission, but is not required.
Haywire! (Japanese: , Kyōki) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Rosie at the Biahno Water-Purification Plant in Primordia, after completing Good Neighbors.

Hair Apparent (Japanese: , Nyepon no Shōnin, The Nyepon Merchant) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Nio at the Dopang Caravan in Sylvalum. This mission is available once the Sapphire Ring has been obtained from the Stray Potamus at Lake Ciel.
Hackers is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is received automatically from Eleonora on the BLADE Concourse during Murderess's Affinity Mission The Little Rich Girl.

Hailing the Chief! is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be accepted at the Mission Control console on the BLADE Concourse in the Administrative District. It leads to the Affinity Mission Mia Grows Up.
Halcyon Days is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located anytime east of Deliverance Park in the Residential District of New Los Angeles between Yelv and Cross.

Herculean Beast Hairs are common materials in . They can be obtained from Dagahn, for 54 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks, or for 35 Material Tickets from the Material Market in . They are also given out as rewards for the Time Attack Mission Beauty and the Beast. They are components in I Thermal Attack Plus and AttributeDmg.THERM augments.

Haven Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Candid & Credible Shield. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Alien Nation. The Haven weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Haven * Iron Haven * Carbide Haven * Ceramic Haven * Cermet Haven * Chrome Haven * Chromoly Haven * Cobalt Haven * Original Haven * Titanium Haven * Ceramic Haven * Diamond Haven

Haven II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Candid & Credible Shield. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Shotgun Diplomacy. The Haven II weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Haven II * Iron Haven II * Carbide Haven II * Ceramic Haven II * Cermet Haven II * Chrome Haven II * Chromoly Haven II * Cobalt Haven II * Titanium Haven II * Original Haven II * Ceramic Haven II * Diamond Haven II

Halting the Ganglion Threat is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.2, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eighteen Pugiliths. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Headwater Protection is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.10, and is unlocked if the Strange Container was opened during The Fierce Electric Fish. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Helna Jacul is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Prone of the Tree Clan. She is the daughter of Bazis Wolfen and Hexuna Nebra. She is born during the events of A New Life. She does not have a physical presence in the game.
Heavy Rain Screen is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X that nullifies the debuffs from heavy rain weather. The Skell equivalent is Weather.HEAVY-RAIN-RES.
Heat Wave Screen is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X that nullifies the debuffs and buffs from heat wave weather.
Heavy Wear is a type of Armor in . This class of armor has much higher defenses than Medium Wear, but comes at a much greater penalty to Gravity Resistance and has limited upgrades.

Heart-to-Hearts are interactions between two playable characters in . Depending on dialog choices, affinity between the involved characters can be either increased or decreased. Heart-to-Hearts also help build character development in the game's storyline. To activate a Heart-to-Heart, the characters must have reached at least the required affinity and both be in the active party. Some Heart-to-Hearts can only be accessed at a certain time of day. It also appears to be required that the Heart-to-Heart of a lower affinity must have been activated already, though this may not always be the case. The scene can still be played out even if the characters have a greater affinity than required, and

The Hardy Aprica is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a level 37 Aprica, and can be found in Cauldros, on a ledge below and southeast of Bestial Utopia. It is accompanied by two level 37 Corpse Sacrifoles. It appears during A Present for Hope after the party speaks to Lularita, and disappears after the Reverend's Journal is obtained. It is not necessary to fight it, and it does not drop any items. If killed, it will respawn 60 seconds later.

Healing is a game mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles. It allows players to use Battle Arts to recover the HP of party members. Specifically, healing Battle Arts are under the Ether Arts category. They scale according to a characters Ether stat, improving their effectiveness. Outside of battles, characters will heal automatically.
